claim: Kadence International's own public methodology summary of 'The TikTok Effect' (June 2023, n=3,400+ TikTok users, 25 non-profits, 9 SEA markets) contains no numeric figure for either '8 million creators' or '63% earning above minimum wage' -- the two numbers TikTok Indonesia and Menekraf Harsya later attributed to this study.
stance_target: the 8-million-creators/63%-above-UMR figure has a traceable, disclosed methodology
scope_conditions: This is the vendor's own summary page, the only publicly accessible methodology-adjacent document located for this study after repeated search attempts across multiple pipeline steps; the full PDF report itself was not locatable via search
quoted_support: Most creators using TikTok as a source of income earn more than the minimum wage in their respective countries, contributing to economic growth.
numbers: 325 million monthly active users in SEA (context figure, not income-related)
region: Southeast Asia (9 markets, not broken out by country in this summary)

claim: The Kadence summary's only quantified findings concern education (91% of educators could promote learning, 92% could share knowledge internationally) and wellness (88% collaborated with NGOs, 91% found supportive community) -- not income, meaning even a generous reading cannot locate the 63% figure's origin in this document.
stance_target: an income-specific percentage figure exists anywhere in the vendor's disclosed summary
scope_conditions: Vendor marketing/knowledge-page summary, not the underlying survey instrument or full technical report; no separate percentages given for the income-related claim
quoted_support: Among surveyed educators, 91% were able to promote online learning to youth through TikTok, and 92% were able to share their knowledge internationally.

claim: The study's stated methodology combined online surveys and offline interviews across a self-selected, non-representative recruitment (existing TikTok users and partner NGOs), which is a convenience/self-selected sample structurally biased toward TikTok-favorable and higher-engagement respondents, independent of whether the 8M/63% figures can be traced to it at all.
stance_target: survivorship/self-selection bias in platform-commissioned creator income studies
scope_conditions: Inferred from stated methodology description; the summary does not disclose a sampling frame, response rate, or recruitment channel in enough detail to fully assess bias magnitude
quoted_support: In partnership with TikTok, Kadence International conducted a survey across nine Southeast Asian (SEA) markets to explore the platform's impact in the region. The study involved over 3,400 TikTok users and 25 non-profit organisations and utilised a mixed methodology of online surveys and offline interviews.
